。它不是「一段一首歌」的結構，而是「一個提示點接一個提示點」的結構。: . It is not structured as a song per section but as one cue after another.
一段音樂可能只有幾秒，用來標記一個進場、一次燈光變化、一句關鍵台詞；也可能長達數: A stretch of music may last only a few seconds, marking an entrance, a lighting change or a key line; it may also run for minutes, accompanying a whole monologue or a passage of physical movement. The music's beginning and end are decided not by phrases but by stage events. So the score carries not only notes but cues: whose line, which light, which move. The players read the score and watch the stage at the same time, and many end up watching the show out of the corner of their eye and listening to the actors with their ears.
一齣戲一週演八場，連續數週，音樂必須在疲勞、場地變化與突發狀況下仍然成立。因此編: A show may run eight performances a week for weeks on end, and the music has to hold up through fatigue, changes of venue and the unexpected. So the arrangement simplifies on purpose: complex harmony reduced to a few key notes, fast figures replaced by patterns that can be repeated, passages that depend on precise ensemble rewritten with some slack. This simplification is not an artistic concession but engineering that lets the music be repeated every day without a slip. Experienced composers think about touring while they write: which parts can be dropped, which passages can be stretched, and where space has to be left for the actors.
主要線條，常兼奏多種樂器: The main line, often doubling several instruments
低音與和聲底: Bass and the floor of the harmony
出現在戲劇製作、實驗劇場、舞蹈劇場、偶戲與戶外演出。曲目是為特定製作寫的，通常不: It appears in plays, experimental theatre, dance theatre, puppet theatre and outdoor performances. The repertoire is written for a particular production and usually never released on its own; the same passage may recur through a whole play, with its instrumentation or tempo adjusted as the drama changes. Some productions put the players on stage and make playing part of the performance; others hide the band at the side of the stage or in the pit so that only the sound appears.
劇場的音響條件通常不如音樂廳，樂手聽到的是經過擴音與監聽的聲音，演員也需要聽到音: The acoustics of a theatre are usually worse than a concert hall's: the players hear amplified and monitored sound, and the actors need to hear the music in order to keep their timing. So bands often use point-to-point monitoring and a handful of microphones rather than a full mixing system — one microphone fewer if possible, one cable fewer if possible. This is the opposite of studio or concert-hall logic, and it has only one purpose: every performance can be set up fast and problems cleared fast.
劇場的預算、舞台空間與移動需求都不允許大編制。小型編制也讓樂手可以看著演員演奏，: Theatre budgets, stage space and the need to move do not allow a large line-up. A small one also lets the players watch the actors as they play, and even take part in the blocking; in experimental theatre the players are sometimes on stage, part of the performance.
劇場音樂就是音樂劇的歌曲。: Theatre music means the songs of a musical.
劇場音樂編制（Theatre Music Ensemble）— 為舞台動作現場演: Theatre Music Ensemble — a small band playing live for stage action, organising the music by cues and scene numbers rather than by song structure. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
劇場音樂編制（theatre music ensemble）是在戲劇或實驗劇場演: The theatre music ensemble is a small band that plays live in a play or an experimental theatre production. It serves not a concert audience but the action and the timing on stage: the music has to follow the actors, follow the lights, follow the rhythm of a scene. The line-up exists because theatre needs a live sound that can be repeated every day, taken on tour and adjusted to conditions on stage, rather than pre-recorded playback.

同一個製作也常同時存在兩種版本：完整版給主要場地，精簡版給巡演或小場地。精簡版會: One production often exists in two versions at once: the full version for the main venue and a reduced one for touring or small spaces. The reduced version drops instruments that are hard to double, turns some passages into playback, or shortens the music so that a few players can carry the whole show. This "same play, different line-up" practice is part of how theatre music works.
和影視配樂編制相比，差別在時間由誰驅動、可否重來。配樂的時間由剪好的畫面與節拍器: Compared with the film scoring session, the difference is what drives the time and whether you can do it again. Scoring's time is locked by picture that has already been cut and by a click, and it can be recorded in sections and patched afterwards; theatre music's time is decided by the actors' actual rhythm, and every performance has to keep up live, with no stopping to try again.
在音樂會裡，樂團決定速度；在劇場裡，演員的節奏決定速度。演員今天講得快一點，音樂: At a concert the band decides the tempo; in the theatre the actors' rhythm decides it. If an actor speaks a little faster tonight, the music has to follow; if an actor adds a stretch of improvisation, the music has to hold or extend. This flexibility does not come from playing freely but from an understanding built in rehearsal: the players know which points can wait and which cannot, the music director gives cues during the performance, and the players stretch or shorten accordingly.
對戲排練、給提示、維持每一場的一致性: Rehearses with the actors, gives cues, keeps every performance consistent
小編制同時是美學與實務的選擇：它讓樂手能看舞台、能移動、能參與表演，也讓巡演與長: A small line-up is an aesthetic choice as well as a practical one: it lets the players see the stage, move about and take part in the performance, and it makes touring and long runs possible. Money is one condition among others, not the only reason.
小編制是因為經費不足。: The line-up is small because there is not enough money.
常與台詞交錯，而不是獨立的歌曲: Often interwoven with the dialogue rather than a song in its own right
找現場錄音或演出紀錄。劇場音樂的版本與演出綁在一起，錄音室重製會失去與舞台對時的: Look for a live recording or a filmed performance. Theatre music's version is bound to the performance, and a studio remake loses the tension of keeping time with the stage.
排練的順序也不同。: The order of rehearsal is different too.
提供短促的聲響與氣氛轉換: Provides short sounds and shifts of atmosphere
提供脈動；也常負責音效型的聲響: Provides the pulse, and often the sound-effect-like noises as well
提示點（cue）是基本單位。: The cue is the basic unit.
最容易被混為一談的是劇場樂池編制。兩者都為舞台伴奏，座位也常在舞台下方或側台；差: The easiest confusion is with the theatre pit. Both accompany the stage and both often sit below it or at the side; the difference is the unit of the music and where the line-up comes from. The pit serves a musical, the music's unit is the song, the line-up is decided by contract and budget, doubling is the core skill, and the timeline is precise to the second; the theatre music ensemble's unit is the cue, the music enters and leaves with the lines, the lights and the blocking, the band is small enough to move about on stage, and simplification and flexibility are what let it be performed every day.
樂團通常先進排練室把音樂練好，再進劇場與演員對戲；但真正的工作發生在對戲的時候：: The band usually learns the music in a rehearsal room first and then moves into the theatre to work with the actors; but the real work happens in that rehearsal with the actors: under which line is the music too loud, which move leaves no time for a cue, which pause needs music to hold it. Many changes are made in the theatre on the spot, with the composer or music director rewriting the score, cutting a section, adding a pause mark. By opening night the score is often very different from the first day of rehearsal.
樂手與演員共享同一個時間。: Players and actors share one time.
每一場都是同一個版本，也都不是。: Every performance is the same version, and none of them is.
注意音樂與台詞的邊界。劇場音樂很少從頭演奏到尾，它進出的位置通常對應舞台事件。: Watch the boundary between music and dialogue. Theatre music rarely plays from beginning to end; where it enters and leaves usually matches a stage event.
注意音量與空間。劇場的擴音通常很節制，音樂要讓台詞清楚，也要在需要時撐住場面。: Notice the volume and the space. Amplification in the theatre is usually restrained: the music has to keep the lines clear, and still hold the scene when it needs to.

為什麼是這樣的人數而不是更多：: Why this many players and no more:
現場樂團只是為了「感覺比較真」，可以用預錄取代。: A live band is only there to feel more real; playback could replace it.
現場演奏的價值在於跟著演員的時間伸縮。預錄音軌無法等演員、無法延長、無法在突發狀: The value of live playing is that it can stretch with the actors' timing. A pre-recorded track cannot wait for an actor, cannot extend, cannot adjust when something unexpected happens, and that is exactly why theatre needs live players.
用少數聲部撐住和聲，同時提供低音的重量: Holds the harmony with a few parts while providing the weight of the bass
編制通常很小，以幾個人組成的小型樂團為常態，因為巡演時每一件樂器、每一個座位、每: The line-up is usually very small, a band of a few players being the norm, because on tour every instrument, every seat and every microphone costs money. The division of work is not by section but arranged around who can, within a limited number of people, cover time, bass, melody and timbre at once. The players double constantly.
聽樂手的兼奏。小型編制裡，同一個人可能在一個樂句之內換樂器，這種切換是編制的特徵: Listen for the doubling. In a small line-up the same player may change instrument within one phrase, and that switching is a feature of the line-up.
聽重複。同一段音樂會在不同場次以不同長度出現，注意它怎麼被延長或縮短。: Listen for the repeats. The same passage appears at different lengths from performance to performance; notice how it is extended or cut short.
與電子原聲混合編制相比，差別在框架放在哪裡。電子原聲編制用固定音軌、即時處理與多: Compared with the electroacoustic ensemble, the difference is where the frame sits. The electroacoustic ensemble builds its frame from fixed tracks, live processing and a multichannel space, and the sound engineer decides where the sound sits; the theatre music ensemble's frame is the stage event and the cue, and the sound is usually restrained, asking only that the lines stay clear and the actors can hear the music.
舞台演出要求每天一致，否則演員無所適從；但演員的狀態、觀眾的反應、場地的聲音每天: A stage performance demands consistency every night, or the actors have nothing to rely on; yet the actors' condition, the audience's response and the sound of the room change from day to day. The music therefore has to provide a stable frame and enough flexibility at the same time. This "floating inside the frame" is the hardest part of theatre music to master: too fixed and it cannot keep up with the stage, too free and the actors lose their support.
這個編制的核心是: At the heart of this line-up is—
這是劇場音樂最特別的地方：音樂不是背景，也不是主角，而是與表演者平行的另一條時間: This is what is most particular to theatre music: the music is neither background nor protagonist but another timeline running parallel to the performers. The two lines have to stay aligned and also allow each other to breathe. When an actor changes the rhythm on the spot, the music has to take it; when the music needs a pause, the actors have to know. This interdependence is built in rehearsal and maintained in performance, by listening to each other afresh every night rather than fixing a version.
音樂劇以歌曲為單位，劇場音樂編制則以提示點為單位，音樂經常沒有歌詞、沒有完整曲式: A musical works in songs; the theatre music ensemble works in cues. The music often has no lyrics and no complete form, and exists for one stage action alone.
音樂必須跟著時間走，而不是帶著時間走。: The music has to follow the time, not carry it.
音響與監聽也是簡化的一部分。: Sound and monitoring are part of the simplification too.
